paragraphs: Making decisions more frequently can make it harder for a reinforcement learning agent to distinguish good actions from bad ones. This paper investigates that problem for distributional reinforcement learning, which represents possible returns as distributions. The authors establish that this richer representation still suffers from sensitivity to decision frequency.

Their theoretical result shows that, as decision frequency increases, the return distribution associated with each action approaches the return distribution of the underlying policy. Action-specific differences therefore shrink. The paper quantifies this collapse and shows that different statistics of the distributions disappear at different rates, making the choice of what to model consequential.

The authors then develop distributional versions of action gaps and advantages, introducing a quantity called superiority that generalizes advantage probabilistically. They build an algorithm around it and evaluate it in option-trading simulations. Those experiments show that properly modeling the superiority distribution improves controllers at high decision frequencies, connecting the theoretical diagnosis to a concrete learning approach.
neurips-2024-action-gaps-and-advantages-.tldr: The paper explains why distributional reinforcement learning struggles at high decision frequencies and introduces a superiority-based algorithm that improves simulated controllers.

paragraphs: CausalStock addresses two obstacles in predicting the movements of multiple stocks: identifying how stocks influence one another and extracting useful signals from noisy news. Relationships such as supplier and customer connections can be directional. A representation that treats both directions alike may therefore miss the structure that the authors seek to capture.

The framework learns temporal causal relationships through a mechanism that accounts for time lags and models a distribution over causal graphs. A Functional Causal Model then uses the discovered relationships to predict stock movements. Alongside this component, a Denoised News Encoder uses large language models' text evaluation abilities to extract useful information from large amounts of news.

Experiments cover six real-world datasets from markets in the United States, China, Japan, and United Kingdom. The authors report better performance than strong baselines for prediction both with and without news. The discovered relationships also offer a potentially clearer account of the prediction mechanism, giving the approach an explanatory role alongside its predictive one.
neurips-2024-causalstock-deep-end-to-end.tldr: CausalStock combines temporal causal discovery with language-model-assisted news filtering to improve multi-stock movement prediction.

paragraphs: Counterfactual fairness asks whether a person's prediction would remain the same if they belonged to a different demographic group. Enforcing this requirement can affect predictive performance, but the size and structure of that trade-off are not automatically clear. This paper studies that relationship theoretically without tying the analysis to a particular model architecture.

The authors propose a method for converting an optimal predictor that may be unfair into a fair predictor with minimal performance loss. The approach combines factual and counterfactual predictions. By analyzing excess risk, the work quantifies the additional prediction error associated with requiring perfect counterfactual fairness, making the cost of that requirement explicit within its theoretical treatment.

The paper also examines the method when causal knowledge is incomplete and develops a practical algorithm for that setting. Experiments on synthetic and semi-synthetic datasets support the analysis and proposed methods. The contribution connects a fairness guarantee to its predictive consequences while also addressing the challenge of applying the approach with only partial causal information.
neurips-2024-counterfactual-fairness-by-.tldr: The paper quantifies the predictive cost of counterfactual fairness and proposes a method for achieving it with minimal performance loss.

paragraphs: Unsupervised skill discovery aims to learn varied behaviors without explicit rewards, but diversity alone does not ensure useful behavior. An agent might learn basic movements while failing to walk or run, or acquire unwanted behaviors such as tripping or entering hazardous areas. DoDont introduces video instructions to guide which skills the agent discovers.

The method has two stages. First, it trains an instruction network from videos that do not include action information. This network learns to distinguish desirable transitions from undesirable ones. Second, the network modifies the reward used during skill discovery, giving the learning process a way to favor behavior consistent with the instructions.

The authors integrate this mechanism into a skill discovery algorithm that maximizes distance, using the instruction network itself as the distance function. In experiments across complex continuous control tasks, fewer than eight instruction videos were sufficient to learn desirable behaviors and avoid undesirable ones. These findings show how a small amount of behavioral guidance can shape otherwise unsupervised skill learning in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2024-do-s-and-don-ts-learning-de.tldr: DoDont uses a small set of instruction videos to steer skill discovery toward desirable behaviors and away from unwanted ones.

paragraphs: Federated learning lets clients train a shared model while keeping their data local. Making performance more equal across clients can require data-rich participants to accept lower performance so others benefit. This creates a participation question: would those clients prefer to leave and form a different coalition?

The paper studies that question through game theory and social choice theory. It models fair federated learning as an altruism coalition formation game, explicitly accounting for how clients value others and how friendship relationships connect them. The analysis links potential instability to these social features, rather than treating equalized performance as automatically destabilizing.

The authors derive optimal bounds on the egalitarian fairness a coalition can achieve while remaining core-stable under different altruistic behaviors. These bounds quantify how achievable fairness relates to differences in local dataset sizes. Experiments examine consistency between the theoretical bounds and empirical fairness. The result is a conditional account of when fairness and stability can coexist, challenging the claim that pursuing egalitarian fairness inevitably causes instability.
neurips-2024-does-egalitarian-fairness-l.tldr: The paper derives fairness bounds for stable federated learning coalitions, showing that egalitarian fairness need not cause instability.

paragraphs: Action detection becomes more demanding when a system must operate online and recognize an open vocabulary of actions. The paper targets this combination, arguing that offline evaluation, fixed action categories, and reliance on manual annotations restrict existing approaches. Its proposed detector, OV-OAD, uses vision-language models and learns solely from text supervision.

The central architectural addition is an object-centered decoder inside a Transformer-based model. Using correspondence between video and text, this decoder aggregates frames with similar meanings. That design connects temporal information in the video to language-based supervision, supporting the paper's goal of zero-shot transfer for online action detection.

Across four action detection benchmarks, OV-OAD outperforms the other advanced zero-shot methods evaluated. The reported results include 37.5% mean average precision on THUMOS’14 and 73.8% calibrated average precision on TVSeries. These findings establish a baseline for combining text-supervised learning with online temporal understanding and support the approach's potential for scalable action recognition in open-world settings.
neurips-2024-does-video-text-pretraining.tldr: OV-OAD uses text supervision and an object-centered Transformer decoder to improve zero-shot online action detection.

paragraphs: Consistency models generate images in one or a few steps, offering a fast alternative to diffusion-based generation. Their speed can come with somewhat lower sample quality. This paper addresses that quality gap through post-processing: it starts with images produced by a consistency model and refines them using an additional learned guide.

The guide combines a classifier and a discriminator in one network, with both parts trained adversarially. The classifier assesses how well an image fits its designated class. The discriminator uses the same network's softmax values to assess proximity to the target data manifold, providing an energy-based signal about how closely the image resembles the intended data.

The method applies projected gradient iterations tailored to each generated example under this joint guidance. On ImageNet at 64-by-64 resolution, the authors report improved FID scores for images produced through both consistency training and consistency distillation. The findings support refinement as a way to improve consistency-generated images, with class assignment and data resemblance contributing complementary guidance.
neurips-2024-enhancing-consistency-based.tldr: A jointly trained classifier and energy-based discriminator guide post-processing that improves the quality of consistency-generated images.

paragraphs: A training dataset may include individual input features without covering every combination that appears at test time. This paper formalizes the resulting challenge for predicting multiple outputs as combinatorial distribution shift. Its focus is on understanding how learning can succeed when the missing coverage concerns combinations of features.

The authors introduce Functional t-Singular Value Decomposition, extending classical tensor decomposition to continuous and infinite feature domains. This gives them a representation for multi-output functions and recasts learning under combinatorial shift as low-rank tensor estimation with data missing not at random. The analysis imposes assumptions on the true functions, training and test distributions, and spectral properties of the underlying embeddings.

Within that framework, the proposed Double-Stage Empirical Risk Minimization algorithm uses different hypothesis classes for different frequency components to accommodate varying spectral decay. The authors establish performance guarantees through theoretical analysis. The contribution is a preliminary foundation for this distribution-shift problem, with its guarantees grounded in the stated structural and distributional assumptions.
neurips-2024-generalized-tensor-decompos.tldr: The paper develops a tensor-based theory and learning algorithm for multi-output prediction when training data omit relevant feature combinations.

paragraphs: Oversmoothing occurs when repeated graph-network layers make node features increasingly alike, erasing distinctions needed for prediction. This paper studies whether that outcome is unavoidable in graph convolutional networks. It analyzes the limit of infinitely many hidden features, where the network can be described through an equivalent Gaussian process.

The theory recovers oversmoothing for typical parameter choices, but also identifies a different phase. When the initial weights have sufficiently large variance, node features can remain informative even at substantial depth. The authors test this prediction in finite-size networks by training a linear classifier on their outputs, linking the infinite-width analysis to finite models.

The paper also extends the idea of information propagation depth to graph convolutional networks. Its analysis predicts that this depth diverges at the boundary between the smoothing and non-smoothing phases, with finite-size experiments showing good agreement. Initializing near that transition produces deep, expressive networks in the reported tests. The finding makes initialization a consequential part of understanding when depth preserves useful node distinctions.
neurips-2024-graph-neural-networks-do-no.tldr: Gaussian-process analysis identifies an initialization-dependent phase in which deep graph convolutional networks preserve informative node features.

paragraphs: Citation prediction usually asks whether one paper will cite another, but references can play very different roles. HLM-Cite focuses on core citations: references that contribute more substantially than a superficial mention. This changes the task into distinguishing core references from both incidental citations and papers that are not cited.

The proposed workflow separates retrieval from reasoning. First, curriculum fine-tuning adapts a text embedding model to retrieve likely core references from a large candidate pool. Then an agentic language-model workflow ranks those retrieved papers through one-shot reasoning about their relationships. This arrangement addresses both the volume of candidate text and the risk that direct prompting relies mainly on surface similarity.

The two-stage pipeline handles candidate sets of 100,000 papers. Evaluation on a dataset spanning 19 scientific fields reports a 17.6% performance improvement over state-of-the-art methods. The findings support combining broad retrieval with focused reasoning when citation importance depends on implicit logical connections between papers, rather than simply whether their topics appear similar.
neurips-2024-hlm-cite-hybrid-language-mo.tldr: HLM-Cite combines embedding-based retrieval with language-model reasoning to identify core scientific citations from large candidate sets.

paragraphs: This paper studies causal effect estimation in bi-directional Mendelian randomization, where two phenotypes may influence one another. The setting is difficult because the data are observational, some candidate instruments are invalid, and unmeasured confounding may be present. Existing approaches often depend on expert selection of instruments or assume a one-directional causal model.

The authors first investigate identifiability: the conditions under which the observational data can determine the causal model. They provide necessary and sufficient conditions for correctly identifying valid instrument sets so that the bi-directional model, including causal directions between the two phenotypes, is identifiable. This makes instrument validity and direction discovery central parts of the analysis.

Using that theory, the paper develops a cluster fusion-like method to discover valid instrument sets and estimate the causal effects of interest. It provides a theoretical correctness result for the algorithm and reports effective estimation in experiments with both one-directional and bi-directional models. The contribution connects conditions for identifying the model to a concrete estimation procedure.
neurips-2024-identification-and-estimati.tldr: The paper establishes identification conditions and an estimation method for bi-directional Mendelian randomization with some invalid instruments.

paragraphs: Distribution Matching Distillation compresses a diffusion model into a fast generator by matching output distributions. However, its original training procedure also uses regression on expensive teacher-generated noise–image pairs. DMD2 removes that requirement, addressing both the cost of constructing those pairs and the restriction imposed by closely following the teacher's sampling paths.

Removing regression destabilizes training because the fake critic estimates the generated distribution insufficiently accurately. DMD2 addresses this with a two-time-scale update rule. It also adds a GAN loss comparing generated images with real data, reducing dependence on imperfect teacher score estimates. For multi-step students, it simulates inference-time generator samples during training to address mismatched training and inference inputs.

Together, these changes achieve reported one-step FID scores of 1.28 on ImageNet-64×64 and 8.35 on zero-shot COCO 2014, surpassing the teacher with a 500-fold reduction in inference cost. Distilling SDXL also produces megapixel images whose reported quality exceeds the teacher's. The results show that distribution matching, real-data training, and better training dynamics can jointly improve speed and quality.
neurips-2024-improved-distribution-match.tldr: DMD2 improves fast image generation by removing costly regression targets, stabilizing distribution matching, and adding real-data adversarial training.

paragraphs: Multilingual tokenization can split non-Latin scripts into excessively small pieces, disadvantaging those languages in efficiency, cost, and utility. MAGNET addresses this over-segmentation by learning where to place boundaries within byte sequences. Its tokenizers are internal model components that predict how bytes should be grouped into subword units.

Earlier gradient-based methods used one boundary predictor and sought uniform compression across sequences, yet still over-segmented non-Latin scripts in multilingual settings. MAGNET instead routes byte sequences through predictors specific to language scripts. Each predictor is optimized for its corresponding script, allowing the segmentation process to account for differences that a single shared predictor may handle unevenly.

The authors report that this modular design reduces disparities in segmentation granularity across scripts. Experiments also show faster language modeling and improved downstream utility. The contribution therefore connects a specific source of multilingual disadvantage—the way text is divided into tokens—to changes in both computational efficiency and model usefulness, with adaptive tokenization providing the mechanism for those improvements.
neurips-2024-magnet-improving-the-multil.tldr: MAGNET learns script-specific token boundaries to reduce multilingual over-segmentation while improving modeling speed and downstream utility.

paragraphs: Endoscopic videos contain complex camera motion, unevenly distributed lesions, and concealed content. Learning useful representations therefore requires attention to both broad video structure and small local details. The paper argues that contrastive pretraining supplies discriminative representations but can leave out fine-grained information needed for pixel-level predictions.

M²CRL combines contrastive learning with masked modeling across multiple views. For global views, an attention-guided tube mask uses attention aggregated across frames to capture spatial and temporal structure. For local views, random tube masking emphasizes local variation. These complementary masking strategies aim to produce representations that distinguish overall content while retaining detailed visual information.

The framework is pretrained on seven public endoscopic video datasets and fine-tuned on three datasets for classification, segmentation, and detection. The authors report improvements over both specialized endoscopic pretraining methods and other self-supervised approaches across these tasks. The findings support combining global discrimination with local perception in a shared pretraining framework, particularly when downstream tasks require different levels of visual detail.
neurips-2024-multi-view-masked-contrasti.tldr: M²CRL combines complementary video masking strategies with contrastive learning to improve endoscopic classification, segmentation, and detection.

paragraphs: A continuously evolving system can still be observed and controlled only at discrete sampling times. This paper studies online learning in that setting for linear systems subject to non-stochastic disturbances. The objective is to learn a controller whose performance is comparable to that of a fixed optimal linear controller despite the disturbances.

The proposed algorithm separates the task into two levels: a higher-level learning strategy and a lower-level feedback control strategy. It achieves sublinear regret, so its accumulated performance gap grows more slowly than the comparison horizon. The authors also provide nonasymptotic results for continuous-time control with finitely many system interactions, making the finite-interaction setting central to the theory.

The paper then examines domain randomization through the same non-stochastic control perspective. Applying its method to Soft Actor-Critic improves results on multiple reinforcement learning tasks in domain-randomized environments. This connects the formal control analysis to empirical agent training, offering both guarantees for the studied linear systems and practical evidence in the reported reinforcement learning settings.
neurips-2024-online-control-with-adversa.tldr: A two-level learning and feedback algorithm achieves sublinear regret for sampled continuous-time linear control under non-stochastic disturbances.

paragraphs: Time-series forecasting involves several distinct needs: predicting a single future value or a distribution of possibilities, over either short or long horizons. Research often concentrates on one combination, such as long-term point prediction. ProbTS asks how that narrow focus shapes conclusions about which methods work well and how broadly those conclusions apply.

The paper introduces a unified benchmark platform for evaluating point and distributional forecasts across prediction horizons. It compares numerous recent methods and analyzes the data characteristics associated with different forecasting requirements. This helps explain why a method favored by one research setting may not fully address the range of forecasting needs considered.

The authors also examine universal forecasting models and find that their analysis of methodological strengths and weaknesses remains relevant to those models. The contribution is a broader evaluation framework and a comparative account of forecasting approaches. It makes the combination of prediction type and horizon part of the assessment, providing a basis for understanding current limitations and identifying future research directions.
neurips-2024-probts-benchmarking-point-a.tldr: ProbTS evaluates forecasting methods across point and distributional predictions and short and long horizons to reveal their differing strengths.

paragraphs: When evaluating an objective is expensive, optimization should make good use of each observation. This paper considers objectives whose values stay unchanged under a known group of transformations. It shows that standard and constrained Bayesian optimization can use observations inefficiently when they fail to incorporate this known structure.

The proposed method builds group invariances into the kernel of the Gaussian process used to predict objective values. The resulting optimization algorithms can exploit those invariances when selecting evaluations. The authors bound the maximum information gain of the invariant kernels and derive upper and lower bounds on the observations needed to reach a specified level of near-optimality.

Experiments show improved sample efficiency on synthetic invariant and approximately invariant functions. Incorporating only part of the invariance achieves similar gains at substantially lower computational cost in the reported tests. The method is also applied to designing a current drive system for a nuclear fusion reactor, finding a high-performance solution where the evaluated non-invariant approaches failed.
neurips-2024-sample-efficient-bayesian-o.tldr: Encoding known transformation invariances in Gaussian-process kernels makes Bayesian optimization more sample-efficient in theory and reported applications.

paragraphs: Satellite network operation depends on knowing traffic conditions, but measuring an entire large, rapidly changing network creates substantial overhead. Satformer tackles the alternative of estimating global traffic from partial measurements. The paper identifies nonlinear relationships across space and time as a central challenge for approaches based on low-rank linear decomposition.

Its proposed solution uses adaptive sparse spatio-temporal attention. The mechanism concentrates attention on selected local regions of the traffic tensor, increasing sensitivity to details and patterns within the measurements. This design aims to capture the nonlinear spatial and temporal relationships that are difficult to represent through the linear decomposition methods discussed in the paper.

Experiments use datasets for small, medium, and large satellite networks. The authors report lower estimation errors and better robustness than mathematical and neural baselines, with especially strong benefits for larger networks. These findings support the proposed attention mechanism as a way to reconstruct network-wide traffic from limited observations and suggest potential for deployment in actual systems.
neurips-2024-satformer-accurate-and-robu.tldr: Satformer uses adaptive sparse attention to estimate satellite network traffic more accurately and robustly from partial measurements.

paragraphs: Learning-rate tuners often use loss curvature, especially the largest Hessian eigenvalue, called sharpness. But sharpness changes during training, and the learning rate itself influences those changes. This paper studies that feedback loop, asking whether a step that immediately reduces loss most effectively also supports good longer-term training.

In full-batch training, the authors find that classical tuners can achieve greater one-step loss reduction yet ultimately underperform constant learning rates. Their explanation is that these tuners disrupt the stabilization of sharpness. A simplified model of learning-rate and curvature dynamics motivates Curvature Dynamics Aware Tuning, which prioritizes longer-term curvature stabilization over immediate objective improvement.

In the full-batch setting, the proposed method behaves similarly to predefined warm-up schedules and outperforms tuned constant learning rates on deep learning objectives. In minibatch training, stochasticity complicates the feedback and helps explain why some existing tuners succeed at suitable batch sizes. The findings make training dynamics, including batch-dependent effects, central to assessing curvature-based learning-rate adaptation.
neurips-2024-stepping-on-the-edge-curvat.tldr: CDAT tunes learning rates to stabilize long-term curvature dynamics, improving full-batch training over tuned constant learning rates.

paragraphs: This paper studies bandit learning when losses can be negative, unbounded, and heavy-tailed. The learner does not know whether loss distributions remain fixed or change adversarially over time. The analysis assumes known parameters bounding the losses' (1+v)-th raw moments, with v between zero and one, rather than requiring bounded losses.

The proposed algorithm gives high-probability regret guarantees in both environments. Its worst-case adversarial regret has a T^(1/(1+v)) dependence, while its stochastic regret has logarithmic dependence on T and depends on the gaps between options. These guarantees strengthen earlier expected-regret results while removing a technical distributional assumption that the authors describe as difficult to verify.

The relaxed assumption also yields a near-optimal result for adversarial heavy-tailed bandits with Huber contamination. A further implication covers bounded true losses protected by pure local differential privacy, again with high-probability guarantees. The contribution combines adaptation to the unknown environment with stronger probabilistic control under the paper's stated moment assumptions.
neurips-2024-taming-heavy-tailed-losses-.tldr: The paper provides high-probability bandit regret guarantees for both stochastic and adversarial heavy-tailed losses under known moment bounds.

paragraphs: In class-incremental learning, a model encounters classes over time but must eventually classify examples across all classes it has seen. At test time, it receives no task identifier to narrow that choice. This creates task confusion, which the paper treats as a central obstacle requiring its own mathematical explanation.

The authors introduce a framework that compares discriminative and generative modeling in this setting. Within that framework, their Infeasibility Theorem shows that task confusion prevents discriminative modeling from achieving optimal class-incremental learning. Their Feasibility Theorem establishes that generative modeling can overcome task confusion and achieve the optimum. These results distinguish the capabilities of the two modeling approaches in the formal treatment.

The paper then uses its framework to assess regularization, bias correction, replay, and generative classifiers. Its analysis suggests that generative modeling is essential for optimal class-incremental learning, whether used to generate replay data or to classify directly. The contribution is a theoretical explanation linking task confusion to the modeling choices behind these learning strategies.
neurips-2024-task-confusion-and-catastro.tldr: A mathematical framework identifies task confusion as a barrier to optimal discriminative class-incremental learning and establishes feasibility through generative modeling.

paragraphs: Cognitive diagnosis estimates students' proficiency in particular knowledge concepts from their interactions with exercises. In practice, many students complete only a small number of exercises, leaving sparse evidence for those estimates. This paper addresses the concern that such sparsity can make diagnoses both inaccurate and unfair.

The proposed CMCD framework augments data using the monotonicity assumption identified by the authors as a fundamental principle in cognitive diagnosis. It turns that assumption into two constraints governing augmentation. These constraints are designed to work with most cognitive diagnosis backbones, so the approach can support a range of existing models rather than depending on one particular architecture.

The authors provide theoretical analysis supporting accuracy and convergence-speed guarantees for CMCD. Experiments on real-world datasets report accurate and fair diagnostic results while addressing sparse interaction data. The contribution ties augmentation to a stated educational assumption, using it to structure additional training information and improve diagnosis in the evaluated settings where observations per student are limited.
neurips-2024-towards-accurate-and-fair-c.tldr: CMCD uses monotonicity-constrained data augmentation to improve the accuracy and fairness of cognitive diagnosis with sparse student interactions.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can provide learned priors for recovering signals from incomplete or corrupted observations. The paper argues that existing optimization-based approaches mainly use those priors while leaving the models' denoising capability underused. ProjDiff aims to bring both capabilities into the same optimization procedure for noisy inverse problems.

The method introduces an auxiliary variable representing a noisy sample at an equivalent step in the diffusion process. This reformulates the inverse problem as constrained optimization over two variables. It then uses projected gradient descent, truncating the gradient through the diffusion model's μ-predictor to solve the resulting problem efficiently.

This construction gives the pretrained model's denoising behavior an explicit role in the optimization, alongside its prior information. Experiments span image restoration, source separation, and partial generation, covering both linear and nonlinear inverse problems. The authors report superior performance across the evaluated problems. These findings support the reformulation as a way to make fuller use of an existing diffusion model when solving reconstruction and generation tasks.
neurips-2024-unleashing-the-denoising-ca.tldr: ProjDiff reformulates inverse problems to use both the learned prior and denoising capability of a pretrained diffusion model.

paragraphs: CLIP can classify images through text prompts without task-specific training examples, but its generalization can weaken when the input domain changes. WATT addresses this through test-time adaptation, using the images encountered during testing to update the model. Its design combines variation in text prompts with averaging of adapted model weights.

The method uses multiple prompt templates and treats predictions as pseudo labels for model updates. Weight averaging then consolidates the information learned through those updates. A separate text ensemble combines diverse textual cues at prediction time, making prompt diversity useful both within the adaptation process and in the final predictions.

The authors report improvements across datasets covering a range of domain shifts, including corrupted image datasets and other challenging settings. The approach requires neither additional model transformations nor new trainable modules. It also operates effectively with a single image in the reported evaluation. These findings support combining pseudo-label updates, weight averaging, and text ensembling as a practical adaptation strategy for CLIP.
neurips-2024-watt-weight-average-test-ti.tldr: WATT adapts CLIP at test time using diverse prompts, pseudo labels, weight averaging, and text ensembling, including in single-image settings.

paragraphs: WildVision evaluates vision-language models through human preferences in real-world multimodal interactions. Its online arena collects user judgments, while a smaller benchmark draws 500 selected examples from 8,000 submissions. The goal is to make benchmark evaluation more closely reflect the preferences observed when people actually interact with these models.

The benchmark uses GPT-4 to judge comparisons between each evaluated model and Claude-3-Sonnet. Its rankings achieve a Spearman correlation of 0.94 with the arena's Elo rankings, exceeding the reported alignment of MMVet, MMMU, and MMStar. This result supports the benchmark's ability to track the human-preference ordering collected by the arena.

An analysis of 20,000 real-world interactions also identifies weaknesses in strong models. GPT-4V performs well relative to several others on simple recognition and reasoning, yet struggles with subtle context, spatial reasoning, visual imagination, and expert knowledge. The study additionally finds hallucination and safety problems under intentional provocation. Together, the preference benchmark and failure analysis provide complementary views of model performance.
neurips-2024-wildvision-evaluating-visio.tldr: WildVision builds a human-preference arena and aligned benchmark while documenting vision-language model failures in real-world interactions.
